title: Indian wedding guest outfits for women
description: What to wear to the mehendi, haldi, sangeet, wedding and reception. Outfit formulas at three budgets, with real brands and prices.
intro: A wedding is five outfits, not one. Each event has its own colour and its own mood. This guide gives you a formula for each, at three budgets. Pick the one that sounds like you. Then repeat the pieces in new ways so the wardrobe stays small.

sections.heading: The rules that hold for every event
sections.body: Start with the bride. Never wear white, ivory or anything close to her lehenga colour. Then ask one question: day or night? Day events want soft light colour and breathable cotton. Night events want depth, shine and structure. Silhouette does the rest. A fitted blouse with a flowing skirt gives you a clear waist and movement. A long straight kurta with a wide palazzo gives you length and ease. Both are good. Choose by how much you plan to dance.
tips: Match colour to event: bright and cotton for mehendi, yellow and pastel for haldi, jewel tones for sangeet, rich and traditional for the ceremony.
Wear one hero piece per outfit: the dupatta, the blouse or the jewellery. Keep the other two quiet.
Check the dress code on the invite. "Traditional" means no gowns. "Indo-western" means you can mix.
Carry a stole or shawl for AC halls. They run cold at night.

sections.heading: Silhouette and colour, event by event
sections.body: Silhouette is the shape of the outfit. Colour is what makes it yours. For a long ceremony, choose a column line: a saree, or a long kurta with straight pants. It looks calm and stays comfortable. For a dance night, choose volume at the hem: a flared lehenga or a full skirt. If you are petite, keep the top and bottom close in colour so the line stays long. If you are tall, you can carry a contrast dupatta or a wide border. For colour, hold the fabric under your chin in daylight. If your skin looks brighter, keep it. If it looks tired, move the colour away from your face and use it in the skirt instead.
tips: Warm skin tones: mustard, terracotta, olive, coral and gold.
Cool skin tones: plum, emerald, sapphire, rose and silver.
Neutral: dusty pink, teal and wine work almost everywhere.
Repeat one colour across two events to cut cost.

sections.heading: Mehendi and haldi
sections.body: Mehendi is green, orange, pink and fun. You sit on the floor, so pick fabric that moves. Haldi is yellow, and you will get stained. Wear something you can afford to ruin, in marigold, mustard or cream with a print. Avoid pure white at haldi. It looks like a dare.

looks.name: Mehendi, easy
pieces: Cotton printed kurta set in green or coral, about ₹1,800 (Libas)
Dupatta in contrast colour, included in set
Footwear: flat kolhapuris, about ₹700 (Fabindia)
Accessory: oxidised jhumkas, about ₹400 (Myntra)
looks.why: A printed cotton set looks festive and survives sitting on the floor.

looks.name: Haldi, soft and bright
pieces: Mustard or marigold anarkali with gota trim, about ₹3,500 (Biba)
Chanderi dupatta in cream, about ₹1,200 (Fabindia)
Footwear: embroidered juttis, about ₹1,200 (Ajio)
Accessory: fresh flower hair clip or real flowers, about ₹300
looks.why: Yellow near the face works on most skin tones, and the trim keeps it dressed.

looks.name: Mehendi, statement
pieces: Hand-block printed lehenga in coral and green, about ₹9,000 (Global Desi / Fabindia Premium)
Cropped cotton-silk blouse, about ₹1,800
Footwear: block-heel mojaris, about ₹2,500 (Ajio)
Accessory: layered kundan choker, about ₹2,500 (Nykaa Fashion)
looks.why: You wear a lehenga without stepping into bridal territory.

sections.heading: Sangeet and cocktail
sections.body: Sangeet is the dance night. You want movement, shine and shoes you can survive in. Jewel tones photograph well under stage lights: emerald, wine, sapphire, plum. Sequins are welcome. If you want a fusion option, a draped saree-gown or a co-ord set with a long jacket works well.

looks.name: Sangeet, fusion
pieces: Sequin blouse top with a flowy satin skirt, about ₹4,000 (Zara or Mango)
Long matching jacket or cape, about ₹2,000 (W)
Footwear: block heels, about ₹1,800 (Ajio)
Accessory: statement chandbalis, about ₹900 (Nykaa Fashion)
looks.why: You can dance in it, and the jacket comes off when the floor gets hot.

looks.name: Sangeet, traditional
pieces: Embroidered lehenga in wine or emerald, about ₹10,000 (Libas or Global Desi)
Net dupatta pinned on one shoulder
Footwear: embellished flats, about ₹1,500
Accessory: maang tikka and studs, about ₹2,000
looks.why: A one-shoulder dupatta keeps your arms free for dancing.

sections.heading: Ceremony and reception
sections.body: The ceremony runs long. Pick silk or a heavy cotton-silk saree in a deep colour that is not red. Red belongs to the bride. Receptions are the most dressed-up night. Gowns, sarees with a modern blouse, and structured lehengas all work here.
tips: Learn one saree drape that stays put for six hours. Practice it before the day.
Use a safety pin kit and a blouse with hooks at the front. You will thank yourself at 11 pm.

sections.heading: Climate note
sections.body: Wedding season in India runs October to February in most of the north, and the rest of the year in the south. North India nights are cold in December. Carry a shawl. Coastal weddings in Kerala or Goa are humid, so pick cotton, chanderi or light georgette. Avoid heavy velvet there.

sections.heading: What to stop buying for weddings
sections.body: Stop buying a new outfit for every event. Buy one good lehenga skirt and three blouses or dupattas. Stop buying full-embroidered heavy sets that you can wear once. Stop buying cheap polyester sarees with sequins that itch and do not drape. Rent or borrow the very expensive piece.

faq.q: What colour should I not wear to an Indian wedding?
faq.a: Avoid white, ivory and any shade close to the bride. Avoid black at the ceremony in many families, though it is fine at a cocktail night. Red is the bride's colour in most communities.

faq.q: What do I wear to a sangeet?
faq.a: Wear something you can dance in. A lehenga, a co-ord set with a jacket, or a draped saree-gown work well. Choose jewel tones or metallics.

faq.q: Can I wear a saree to a day wedding?
faq.a: Yes. Pick cotton silk, chanderi or organza in a soft colour. Skip heavy zari in daylight. It reads as too much.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a wedding guest outfit?
faq.a: Most people spend between ₹2,000 and ₹6,000 per event. Spend more on the ceremony and reception, and less on mehendi and haldi.
